Using skis borrowed from Italy's Sofia Goggia, Shiffrin was fifth after the downhill run with lower-ranked slalom skiers ahead of her. But her frustrations continued as, after 10 gates in the slalom, she fell again to complete her individual campaign without a medal.\n\nDetermined to take something from the Games, Shiffrin lined up for the mixed team parallel event but won just one of four races with USA eventually losing the small final for bronze against Norway.\n\n\"Day after day, I just kept making the decision that I wanted to keep going, keep trying,\" she said. \"It's always been a dream of mine to compete in every event at the Olympic Games. \u0026ndash; Arianna Fontana finally secured a gold in her fourth Games, PyeongChang 2018, in the 500m. Arianna took home three medals (bringing her total to eight) to become the most decorated female short track speed skater in Olympic history.\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch5\u003eNo limits\u003c/h5\u003e\u003cp\u003eOn 10 December 2017, Arianna Fontana, named flagbearer for Italy at the PyeongChang Games, posted a photo of herself as a child on Instagram, wearing skates, a ski suit, knee pads and a short track helmet, and wrote: \"I remember the exact moment that I decided to follow my passion. It is easy to remember, because I have thought of this moment every time I have been doubted, every time I was told that I wouldn't make it. It is in these moments that I have found the strength and the motivation to push myself and to realise that there are no limits, only in our imagination. Limits imposed by other people are not for me nor for those who remain committed to their vision.\" Born in Sondrio, in the Valtellina valley (Lombardy), Arianna began in her discipline at age four, following in the footsteps of her older brother. The talent she showed from an early age saw her join the Italian team at age 15 and promptly mount three podiums (500m, 1,500m and 3,000m) to give her second place overall at the European Championships in Krynica-Zdr\u0026oacute;j (Poland). Full speed ahead to Turin 2006!\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch5\u003eThe youngest ever Italian to medal at the Winter Games\u003c/h5\u003e\u003cp\u003eOn the ice in the Palavela arena in Turin, in front of a home audience, Arianna was eliminated in the quarter-final of the 500m and the semi-final of the 1,000m, from which she went on to place third in the B final, for sixth place overall. And on 22 February 2006, she competed in the final of the 3,000m relay with Marta Capruso, Katia Zini and Mara Zini. South Korea took gold and, with China disqualified, Canada secured silver and Italy bronze. At age 15 and 314 days, Arianna became the youngest ever Italian to win an Olympic medal at the Winter Games. As such, the young skater was named a Knight of the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch5\u003eMaking history for Italy at Vancouver 2010\u003c/h5\u003e\u003cp\u003eDetermined to do all she could to close the technical gap separating her from the best Korean and Chinese skaters, Arianna won her first world medal at the 2007 World Championships in Milan (silver in the 500m) and shone on the European stage by winning the overall title in both 2008 and 2009, as well as a total of eight European gold medals in the period to 2010. At the Vancouver Winter Games, in the majestic Pacific Coliseum, the champion from Bormio Ghiaccio ASD was eliminated in the quarter-final of the 1,000m, finished third in the semi-final of the 1,500m and then ninth overall after winning the B final. The Italian 3,000m relay team also went out in the semi-final and did not perform well in the B final. But after a brilliant performance in the 500m, Arianna battled it out in the final on 17 February, maintaining third place throughout the race to take bronze behind Canada's Marianne St-Gelais (silver) and China's Wang Meng (gold). She became the first Italian to win an Olympic medal in a women's individual short track skating event.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch5\u003eRepeated successes\u003c/h5\u003e\u003cp\u003eIn 2011, 2012 and 2013, Arianna reaffirmed her status as the unbeatable European champion by winning the overall title in the European Championships in Heerenveen (Netherlands), Mlad\u0026aacute; Boleslav (Czech Republic) and Malm\u0026ouml; (Sweden). She also claimed her first overall bronze at the World Cup in Sheffield (United Kingdom) \u0026ndash; with two silver medals in the 500m and 1,000m \u0026ndash; and her second in Shanghai (China) the following year. In addition, she finished the 2011-2012 season at the top of the World Cup overall standings for the 500m, something which the Italian had not previously achieved. She explained in January 2014: \"I aim to arrive at Sochi in peak physical and mental condition. I will attempt to make it to the finals of all distances, including the relays, and I will try for the medal each time.\" An Olympic target that she very nearly met!\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThree podium places at Sochi 2014\u003cbr /\u003eIn the space of five days, from 13 to 18 February 2014, Arianna did not step down from the podium in Sochi's Iceberg arena. It all started with an incredible 500m final: four laps from the finish, British skater Elise Christie took down Arianna and Park Seung-hi (South Korea) in a group crash behind Li Jianrou (China). The Chinese skater continued the race alone and took gold. The other three finalists picked themselves up and Christie crossed the line in second place, in front of Arianna. The Brit was then disqualified and the Italian awarded the silver medal, which, in her words, \"felt like gold\". Two days later, during the 1,500m final, a crash at the back of the field eliminated three of the seven skaters. Arianna maintained her position behind Shim Suk-hee (South Korea) and Zhou Yang (China) to cross the line for bronze. Finally, on 18 February, China was disqualified after the 3,000m relay, putting the Italian team (Arianna, Lucia Peretti, Martina Valcepina and Elena Viviani) \u0026ndash; who crossed the line fourth \u0026ndash; on the third step of the podium, which was topped by the South Korean team. But Arianna fell one event short of reaching her goal, after being given a penalty in the quarter-final of the 1,000m.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch5\u003eA break before her fourth Winter Games\u003c/h5\u003e\u003cp\u003eWith four Olympic medals by the age of 23, Arianna took a long break beginning in 2015. \"I was pretty tired mentally. My body was ready to race again but my mind was not. I had some doubts on whether to keep skating or not.\" During her time away from the ice, she took up boxing! When she returned to competition, qualifying for her fourth Winter Games in PyeongChang, she resumed her European dominance with new overall victories in Turin in 2017 and Dresden in 2018, one month before the Winter Games. Her European medal total reached 41 podium places and 24 titles, including seven overall wins.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch5\u003eGold finally, and the record too!\u003c/h5\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe 2018 PyeongChang Winter Games turned into a fairy tale for the 27-year-old champion. After carrying the Italian flag in the Opening Ceremony, Arianna finally reached her goal: on 13 February, in the packed Gangneung arena, she led the 500m final from start to finish, then held out against Choi Min-jeong to cross the line a skate's length (22cm) ahead of the South Korean, who was later disqualified for obstruction. The Italian's sixth Olympic medal was gold! \"When I saw I was first, I was just yelling and started crying. I worked for four years, and the last four months were really hard for me. I was really focused on getting here in the best shape ever. I have been chasing gold and, finally, I have it,\" she said.\u003cbr /\u003e\u003cbr /\u003eAfter placing seventh, and last, in the 1,500m final won by Choi, Arianna took the silver medal with Lucia Peretti, Cecilia Maffei and Martina Valcepina in the 3,000m relay, despite being caught up in a crash. Italy were the only team to officially finish behind South Korea; the other two teams \u0026ndash; China and Canada \u0026ndash; were disqualified, meaning that the Dutch team, winners of the B final, took bronze. Finally, two days later, Fontana won her eighth Olympic medal after finishing third in the 1,000m final won by the Dutch skater Suzanne Schulting, with silver going to the Canadian Kim Boutin. In four Olympic Games, Arianna Fontana has won a total of one gold medal, two silver medals and five bronze medals: she is the most decorated female short track skater of all time, equalling the records of the American Apolo Anton Ohno (two gold, two silver and four bronze) and the South Korean then Russian Viktor An (six gold and two bronze).\u0026nbsp;\u003cbr /\u003e\u003cbr /\u003eAfter leaving some doubt as to her possible retirement from the sport, Arianna announced at the end of May 2018 that she intends to continue competing. \"It is time to resume training, to get in shape, to make plans for the years ahead, which will take me to the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics,\" she said. <p>India will head to the continental showpiece looking to build on its record-breaking campaign at <a href="https://www.olympics.com/en/news/asian-games-2023-hangzhou-india-medals-tally-winners-table" data-tracking-payload="{"implementation_provider":"sed","content_geography":"BD,BT,IN,MV,NP,PK,LK","content_id":"24a6f5d0-b792-4d3e-811a-d295950360b2","content_release_date_local_utc":"2026-08-11T13:35:31.012Z","content_title":"India's Asian Games 2026 squad: Athletes and teams who made the cut for Aichi-Nagoya - full list","tag":"[\"newsclip\",\"noc-in\",\"sportzinteractive\",\"gender-mixed\",\"multisport\",\"ali-asgar-nalwala\"]","module_type":"TextBlock","module_title":"India's Asian Games 2026 squad: Athletes and teams who made the cut for Aichi-Nagoya - full list","section_level_1":"news","section_level_2":"indian-athletes-qualified-asian-games-2026-aichi-nagoya","discipline":"multisport","odf_id":"","module_instance":"Inline","module_id":null}" data-tracking="click">Hangzhou 2023</a>, where the country won 107 medals - 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze.</p>

Picture by BAI By Ali Asgar Nalwala The Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, will be held from September 19 to October 4, with 45 countries and regions set to compete across 43 sports. India will head to the continental showpiece looking to build on its record-breaking campaign at Hangzhou 2023 , where the country won 107 medals - 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze. Despite Neeraj Chopra withdrawing from the Asian Games after an ankle injury, India's Aichi-Nagoya 2026 contingent will still feature five individual Olympic medallists . PV Sindhu ( badminton ), Manu Bhaker ( shooting ), Lovlina Borgohain ( boxing ), Aman Sehrawat ( wrestling ) and Mirabai Chanu ( weightlifting ) are expected to be among the country's major medal contenders. In cricket , Shreyas Iyer will lead India's title defence at the T20 competition, with teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also included. The Indian women's cricket team, also defending champions, will be led by Harmanpreet Kaur. Hockey will have added significance in Aichi-Nagoya, with the men's and women's tournaments serving as continental qualification events for the LA 2028 Olympics . The winners of the Asian Games hockey competitions will earn direct qualification for LA 2028. Anahat Singh will also return to the Asian Games after helping India win a women's team bronze in squash at Hangzhou 2023. She also won a mixed doubles bronze at the Games alongside Abhay Singh. Squash offers Olympic quotas in singles events. Here is the list of Indian sportspersons and teams who have been selected or have qualified for the Asian Games 2026 so far. Athlete list is subject to change.             <h1 class="section--title">INTERNATIONAL OLYMPIC COMMITTEE - PRIVACY POLICY</h1>
        </div>

        <div class="section--content b2p-col__12">
<p>This Privacy Policy, as updated from time to time, explains how the International Olympic Committee (“<strong>IOC</strong>”) processes personal data in the context of its digital activities. For example, websites, mobile applications, connected TV applications, digital marketing, online professional services and business resources, as well as fan engagement initiatives and online registration features that are managed by the IOC alone or in cooperation with other members of the Olympic Movement. We refer to these activities as the “<strong>Services</strong>” in this Privacy Policy.</p>

<p>It also details how the IOC processes the personal data that it receives from other organisations, or via cookies and similar technologies that are integrated into another organisation’s digital properties for the benefit of the IOC.</p>

<p>Other organisations may launch and operate websites, newsletters, e-commerce platforms or other services that are (a) related to the Olympic Games, Youth Olympic Games or to the Olympic Movement’s activities, or (b) feature Olympics-related content. Such sites and services are operated independently from the IOC and are not covered by this Privacy Policy. We therefore encourage you to read the terms of use and privacy policies that are applicable to those sites and services. If we collect or otherwise receive personal data through them, this will be indicated in the site’s or service owner’s privacy policies and/or terms of use.</p>
<p><strong>PRIVACY POLICY UPDATE: This Privacy Policy was last updated on 14 July 2026. It has been updated to reflect the following material changes:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li><strong>We have introduced new additions regarding email pixel tracking. Please see the section titles “Email Tracking Pixels” contained below.</strong></li>
<li><strong>The Privacy Policy has been updated to clarify that third party services may be accessed through links or through content and features made available within our Services. It also clarifies that when users choose to interact with those third party services, their personal data may be collected and processed by the third parties in accordance with their own privacy practices.</strong></li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Who are we?</strong></h3>

<p>When we refer to ‘<strong>’we’’</strong>, ‘<strong>’our’’</strong> or “<strong>us</strong>” in this Privacy Policy, we mean the IOC. The Privacy Policy also covers those instances where the IOC and the Olympic Foundation for Culture and Heritage (the “<strong>Foundation</strong>”), or the IOC and an Organising Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Games (an “<strong>OCOG</strong>”) process data jointly. Annexes 2 and 3, as updated from time to time, provide further details on such joint data processing.</p>

<p>The IOC is a private, not-for-profit, international organisation recognised to be of public interest by the Swiss authorities and constituted in the form of a Swiss law association, having its registered office in Maison Olympique (Olympic House) 1007 Lausanne, Switzerland. The mission of the IOC is to promote Olympism throughout the world, to lead the Olympic Movement and to ensure the regular celebration of the Olympic Games. To learn more about the IOC, its goals and activities, please consult the <a href="https://olympics.com/en/cookie-policy" target="_blank">Olympic Charter</a> and the <a href="https://olympics.com/ioc/principles" target="_blank">IOC Principles</a>.</p>

<p>The Foundation (with address Quai d’Ouchy 1, 1006 Lausanne, Switzerland) manages the Olympic Museum and the Olympic Studies Centre in Lausanne, Switzerland.</p>

<p>An OCOG is responsible for organising an edition of the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games. Each OCOG is based in the territory in which its respective Olympic and Paralympic Games shall be hosted.</p>

<p>When we refer to “<strong>you</strong>” or “<strong>your</strong>” we mean those individuals whose data we collect through the Services, or whose data we receive from other organisations that we work with.</p>
<h3><strong>Our role in the processing of personal data</strong></h3>

<ol>
<li><h4><strong>Data collected via the Services</strong></h4></li>
</ol>

<p>The IOC is an independent data controller of the personal data that is collected through the Services <strong>except</strong>:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>where the user-facing information (which includes information about cookies) provided in relation to the Services states otherwise;</p></li>
<li><p>where data is collected through a graphical user interface that is displayed on our Services but which is managed by another commercial organisation. Please see the section below entitled ‘<strong>Third Party Environments</strong>’ for more information;</p></li>
<li><p>where the Services relate to the Olympic Museum (in particular <a href="https://olympics.com/museum" target="_blank">https://olympics.com/museum</a>, <a href="https://museumshop.olympics.com/">https://museumshop.olympics.com</a>), the Olympic Studies Centre (in particular <a href="https://olympics.com/ioc/olympic-studies-centre">https://olympics.com/ioc/olympic-studies-centre</a>, <a href="https://library.olympics.com/" target="_blank">https://library.olympics.com/</a>) and other activities of the Foundation. In which case, your personal data will be processed by the IOC and the Foundation for the purposes detailed in Annex 2, acting as joint controllers; or</p></li>
<li><p>where the IOC is engaged in digital activities with other organisations within the Olympic Movement, such as OCOGs. In which case, Annex 3 of this Privacy Policy (or the privacy information presented at the point of data collection) details each organisation’s controllership of the data involved.</p>

<ol start="2">
<li><h4><strong>Data collected via third party sites and services</strong></h4></li>
</ol></li>
</ul>

<p>Where the IOC receives personal data that has been collected by other organisations, or where personal data is collected through IOC-owned or procured technologies or features deployed by other organisations on their digital services, the IOC is a data controller of that data.</p>

<p>This applies to personal data that is collected via websites and other digital services owned or operated by:</p>

<ul>
<li>each OCOG (including the Paris 2024 Organising Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Games (“<strong>Paris 2024</strong>”), the Milano Cortina 2026 Organising Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Games (“<strong>MiCo 2026</strong>”) and the Los Angeles 2028 Organising Committee for the Olympic and Paralympic Games ("<strong>LA28</strong>")), and</li>
<li>other organisations within the Olympic Movement, as well as commercial organisations that are permitted to sell and promote Olympic-themed digital services or to use the Olympic Properties.</li>
</ul>

<p>See paragraph 3 “<strong>Collection of data through third parties</strong>” in the section “<strong>What information do we collect?</strong>” (below) as well as Annex 3 for more details.</p>
<h3><strong>What information do we collect?</strong></h3>

<h4><strong>1. Information that you provide to us</strong></h4>

<p>You provide us with information, including personal data, when you use the Services. For example when you sign up for and sign in to a user account, complete certain transactions or subscribe to Services, promotional communications or media alerts. We also collect data when you communicate with us.</p>

<p><strong>a) Information collected when you use the Services</strong></p>

<p>Certain Services require that you provide information about yourself. This is the case, for instance, in respect of the Services that:</p>

<ul>
<li>we make available to other Olympic Movement stakeholders;</li>
<li>are relevant to your registration or accreditation for the Olympic Games, Youth Olympic Games or other events organised by us, as well as the Services through which you may book travel and accommodation related to these events; or</li>
<li>entail a game, contest, sweepstake or other fan engagement opportunity.</li>
</ul>

<p>In these situations and where necessary we will inform you more specifically about the information we need to collect in order to provide you with the requested goods or services and of any other conditions applicable to the processing of this personal data. The information needed will vary depending on the nature of the Services. It may include information such as first name, last name, business organisation, job title, physical address, phone number, nationality, travel and accommodation details, passport or ID card number, credit card information, height and weight information, size of garments or shoes, allergies and food habits.</p>

<p><strong>b) Information collected when you sign up for and sign in to a user account</strong></p>

<p>Individuals such as fans and athletes can register for a user account on the Olympics.com website and associated mobile application. If you use this type of account, we will collect the personal data that you provide to us as well as information that is automatically generated when you sign up for and sign in to the account (for example, data generated through cookies and similar technologies, subject to our Cookie Policy at <a href="mailto:privacy@olympic.org">https://olympics.com/en/cookie-policy</a>, and other information that is generated when you use or interact with the Services). This personal data typically includes your email address, place of residence, age information, password, acceptance of terms and unique identifier, and may include further information such as your preferences and characteristics (i.e. your favourite sports), and a record of any consent that you provide (such as your consent to receive marketing communications).</p>

<p>Certain Services require the collection of additional information. When you create or use an athlete account on the A365 website (https://www.olympics.com/athlete365) or the A365 app (the "<strong>A365 Platform</strong>"), we may collect information that is necessary to verify your identity and to confirm your eligibility as an athlete. Such verification is carried out through designated identity-verification service providers. In this context, personal data processed for identity verification may include the information contained in the identity document you provide (such as your name, date of birth, document number, issuing country and the image of the document), as well as biometric data generated during liveness detection or similar checks (for example, images or video of your face captured in real time to confirm that the document belongs to you).</p>

<p><strong>c) Information collected when you communicate with us</strong></p>

<p>If you communicate with us and/or request any information or service from us, we will use your account information and any other information you may provide to us (such as email address, phone number, and the content of your communication or request) in order to respond to you.</p>

<h4><strong>2. Information that is collected through cookies and similar technologies</strong></h4>

<p>We use automatic tracking mechanisms like cookies and similar technologies to collect certain data while you are browsing our Services, or when you visit the sites or services of other organisations that we work with. A cookie is a small file, stored on your browser or computer hard drive, which is used to collect data about your interactions with websites and other digital properties. For example, information about your device (browser type, operating system, language, unique device identifier), network connections (Internet Service Provider, IP address, time zone), browsing history including date and time and pages visited, as well as general location such as your city and country.</p>

<p>You can disable cookies (except those cookies that are strictly necessary) or manage cookies using the cookies settings available on each of the websites or other digital properties through which the cookies are set. You can also manage cookies by configuring the functionalities of your internet browser.</p>

<p>To know more about our use of cookies on the Services, and how to manage your consent to cookies, please consult our Cookie Policy at <a href="mailto:privacy@olympic.org">https://olympics.com/en/cookie-policy</a>. Where our cookies are placed on third party sites or services, you should consult their cookie policies and consent management tools.</p>

<p>Email Tracking Pixels</p>

<p>When you create an account, subscribe to a newsletter, request information, or otherwise provide your email address, we may send you emails containing tracking pixels or similar technologies. Tracking pixels are small invisible images embedded in certain emails. When an email is viewed, these technologies may collect certain technical information, such as whether the email has been opened, the date and time of access, the type of device used, the email client or software used, and certain associated technical information, including the recipient’s IP address or an approximate location that may be inferred from it. These technologies may be loaded on any device used to access emails sent to the email address you have provided to us, including computers, tablets, and mobile phones. Where required by applicable law, your consent will be obtained before tracking pixels subject to consent are used. We use this information for the purposes listed in the section “How do we use the information we collect". To manage your preference, please use your user account where you may opt out, if we have obtained your consent. The choices you make are associated with the relevant email address and apply to emails sent to that address. You may also withdraw your consent at any time through the link provided in the footer of the relevant emails.</p>

<p>The absence of consent, refusal of consent, or withdrawal of consent for email tracking will not affect your subscription to our newsletters, marketing communications, service updates, or any other communications you have chosen to receive. You will continue to receive such communications in accordance with your communication preferences.</p>

<p>Opting out of email tracking simply means that we will no longer use tracking pixels to collect information about your interactions with our emails, such as whether an email was opened or a link was clicked. As a result, we may be less able to measure the effectiveness of our communications or personalize their content based on your interests and engagement.</p>

<p>Please note that tracking pixels used in emails are distinct from cookies and other tracking technologies used when you browse our website.</p>

<h4><strong>3. Collection of data through third parties</strong></h4>

<p>You can sign up for, or sign in to, a user account with the information of an account you hold with a third party such as Facebook, Google and Apple. If you choose this option, you authorise these organisations to provide us with some of the personal data they hold about you. The personal data shared with us will depend on the third party services that you use to register with us and on the scope of the information you allow those third parties to share, but typically it includes your first name and last name, user name, phone number, unique identifiers and access tokens, e-mail address, date of birth and preferences (e.g. pages you have favourited or saved).</p>

<p>In some scenarios we authorise third parties to launch and operate Olympic-themed digital services or to feature Olympic Properties within their websites or other digital services. For example, the Olympic Shop operated by Fanatics, Inc. and its affiliates under authorisation of the IOC and OCOGs (see, for instance, the EU version of the Olympic Shop here <a href="https://shop.olympics.com/en/">https://shop.olympics.com/en/</a>).  These third parties may share information that they collect about you with us, for example your first and last name or unique identifier, your email address, your stated marketing preferences and data about the webpages you visit and the Olympic-branded goods or services that you purchase. In such cases, the sharing of information with us will be specified in, and carried out in accordance with, the privacy and cookie policies issued by these third parties.</p>

<p>OCOGs, for example Paris 2024, MiCo 2026 and LA28, share the personal data of their users with the IOC. The IOC uses such data for purposes including Olympic Games optimisation, to better understand fans, to evaluate the performance of digital properties or activities connected to the Olympic Games or Paralympic Games, for commercial and operational reporting, to assess, establish and enforce the IOC's and/or the OCOG's rights, including their respective intellectual property rights (e.g. in relation to ticketing, other relevant contractual terms or otherwise), to promote the Olympic Movement, the IOC Marketing Partners and the Olympic Games, or to provide and personalise its Services. In such cases, this sharing of personal data with the IOC will be specified in, and carried out in accordance with, the privacy and cookie policies issued by each of the relevant OCOGs.</p>

<p>Other authorised third parties, such as key partners of the IOC and/or OCOGs involved in the organisation, delivery, or support of the Olympic Games or Paralympic Games (for example, ticketing or access providers, distributors, or hospitality partners), may share personal data with the IOC. This may include your contact details and information relating to the services they provide, to the extent necessary for the purposes described in the section “<strong>How do we use the information we collect?</strong>” (below).</p>

<h4><strong>4. Information manifestly made public</strong></h4>

<p>Content offered on our Services may include information manifestly made public such as competitions and results, biographies about Olympians and other athletes, coaches and other persons involved in the Olympic Games, Youth Olympic Games and other major sports competitions, who are newsworthy and whose stories contribute to the mission of the IOC and the Olympic Movement. This information was disclosed by athletes and other concerned persons in the context of their participation in Olympic Games, Youth Olympic Games and other sports competitions, interviews and other media events, media publications or through other means and was compiled by us, in cooperation with International Federations, National Olympic Committees, Organising Committees for the Olympic Games and Youth Olympic Games and other Olympic Movement stakeholders.</p>

<h4><strong>5. Screening</strong></h4>

<p>We may collect personal data during background checks or other verifications required to meet legal, regulatory, integrity and compliance obligations, or to confirm eligibility and suitability for roles, programmes, or other forms of engagement. This may include information from public registers, details about your position and professional activities, personal and financial history, business background, and contact information.</p>

<h4><strong>6. Recordings and transcriptions</strong></h4>

<p>We may record audio and/or video during online meetings conducted through video-conferencing platforms (such as Microsoft Teams or Zoom). We may also create automated or manual transcripts of these meetings. Any recordings or transcripts may contain personal data, including your image, voice, comments, opinions, reactions, and other information you choose to share during the meeting.</p>

<p>Participants will be informed appropriately before a meeting is recorded. Where legally required, we will obtain your consent prior to recording and/or transcribing.</p>
<h3>How do we use the information we collect?</h3>

<p>We use the information we collect about you and your use of the Services and, where relevant, your use of third party sites and services, to:</p>

<p>a) facilitate your use of the Services, which includes enabling you to register for a user account as well as account authentication and management, and supporting the operation of features that you choose to use;</p>

<p>b) maintain and develop the Services;</p>

<p>c) gather statistics to help diagnose problems, enhance your experience of the Services, improve the quality of the Services and for purposes connected to optimisation of third party sites and services (for example, the sites and services that are managed by OCOGs);</p>

<p>d) ensure the security of the Services and make sure that the Services are used in compliance with our Terms of Service and applicable laws;</p>

<p>e) carry out profiling in order to better understand fans of the Olympic Games, organise (segment) fans into groups that share similar interests and characteristics, and use those groups and the personal data of group members to build audiences for our campaigns.   </p>

<p>We may combine the information that you provide to us with the data that is derived from marketing and advertising cookies (if you have consented to cookies; our Cookie Policy can be found at <a href="https://olympics.com/en/cookie-policy">https://olympics.com/en/cookie-policy</a>), as well as the information we receive from third parties, to build a profile of you. We will also draw inferences about you based on your profile. For example, we might infer your interests (i.e. favourite sport) and characteristics (i.e. preferred language). In such case, and depending upon what you have consented to, we use this information to serve more relevant content and marketing communications to target audiences (which may include you or people with a similar profile to you) via our Services or via platforms that are managed by other organisations;   </p>

<p>f) allow you to participate in any game, contest, sweepstake or other fan engagement opportunity which we make available through the Services or through other organisations that we work with, and for the purposes of administering these initiatives (assessing and confirming the eligibility of participants, awarding prizes to the winners etc.);</p>

<p>g) optimise the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games, including through research, planning, analysis, and statistical activities aimed at improving logistics, services, performance, and the overall experience for athletes, partners, and spectators;</p>

<p>h) promote and raise awareness of the Olympic Movement, the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games, and our marketing partners, including through communications, campaigns, and related promotional activities;</p>

<p>i) provide you goods, services, information, or content that you have requested;</p>

<p>j) communicate with you, including by answering your questions and requests, sending you communications related to your user account and our Terms of Service and, if you have opted-in or where the law otherwise permits, send you marketing communications (including by email and other electronic channels) about the Services, our activities and the activities of the Olympic Movement and its partners, while offering you the possibility to opt-out from such communications at any time;</p>

<p>k) show and measure advertisements on the Services, on third party services like Google, Facebook, and YouTube and on the sites and services of other organisations that we work with. If you are a user of the third party sites and services mentioned in this paragraph (i) as well as a user of our Services, we may, by sharing information with those third parties, serve advertisements to you (or people with a similar profile to you) via their sites and services;</p>

<p>l) carry out internal commercial and operational reporting. This could include analysing trends, assessing the effectiveness of our services and initiatives, and making informed decisions to improve our offerings and operations;</p>

<p>m) assess, investigate and enforce compliance with applicable terms and conditions, including by identifying and reviewing suspicious or potentially unlawful activity related to the purchase, use, distribution, or transfer of tickets or other similar products or services. This may include taking appropriate measures to prevent fraud, unauthorised resale, or other violations of applicable policies or legal requirements;</p>

<p>n) establish, protect, and enforce our rights, including intellectual property and other legal rights. This may involve identifying and investigating potential infringements, taking appropriate legal or other actions to safeguard our rights, and ensuring compliance with applicable terms, policies, and legal requirements;</p>

<p>o) verify the identity of users creating or using an athlete account on the A365 Platform in order to confirm their eligibility and to administer athlete-only or other specific initiatives, including relevant programmes, awards or other benefits that are available only to a specific group of eligible users, such as the Airbnb Athlete Travel Grant ("<strong>AATG</strong>");</p>

<p>p) conduct background checks and other appropriate verifications where necessary to comply with relevant standards, regulations or terms, with our integrity and compliance obligations, or to assess whether individuals or organisations involved in our activities or initiatives (such as candidates, suppliers, athletes, ambassadors, partners, or other third parties) meet the applicable eligibility, suitability, and/or integrity requirements for a particular programme, role, or engagement; and</p>

<p>q) record and, where applicable, transcribe online meetings to document discussions, ensure the accuracy of information, support training and internal collaboration, facilitate follow-up actions, and maintain appropriate records.</p>

<h3><strong>Who do we share your information with?</strong></h3>

<p>We make certain personal data publicly available via the Services or through third party sites and services. For example:</p>

<p>a) where the nature of the Services demand it. Services such as virtual meet-ups and chat forums, online games, contests, or sweepstakes may involve the publication of personal data, such as your audio, visual or written contribution, game play data in league tables or winner announcements; and</p>

<p>b) where the Services feature news stories and other editorial content about, biographies and sports competition results of, Olympians, other athletes, coaches or other persons whose activities are relevant to the IOC’s mission.</p>

<h4><strong>2. The IOC, the Foundation and OCOGs</strong></h4>

<p>The Services are provided by the IOC and, where applicable, the Foundation. We share your personal data among us for the purposes highlighted in this Privacy Policy. Annex 2 of this Privacy Policy provides more information about where the IOC and the Foundation work together to process your personal data.</p>

<p>Where expressly indicated in this privacy policy, we share your personal data with OCOGs. This includes personal data collected through the Services (for example, where you subscribe to receive promotional communications from OCOGs) or by other organisations that we work with.</p>

<p>Annex 3 of this Privacy Policy provides more information about these OCOGs, the situations in which we share personal data with them and the purposes for which they may use such data.</p>

<h4><strong>3. Our service providers</strong></h4>

<p>We rely on a network of professional service providers who are working on our behalf and help us to operate, develop, secure, promote and measure the Services and our advertisements. The services provided by these organisations include, in particular:</p>

<p>a) customer data infrastructure including hosting services, platform development services and general IT services;</p>

<p>b) customer identity and access management, as well as identity-verification services, including athlete identity verification carried out through the A365 Platform;</p>

<p>c) customer services, customer relationship management and other communication-related services including those related to email and push notifications;</p>

<p>d) analytics, audience and advertising measurement services;</p>

<p>e) services related to promotional activities, including third party web and social media services through which we serve our advertisements;</p>

<p>f) services to manage users’ consents and privacy related requests;</p>

<p>g) background checks or screening services.</p>

<p>In order to deliver these services to us, these organisations will process your personal data. These service providers are bound by strict confidentiality obligations. The service providers will retain and use such personal data for as long as they are working for us or until you decide to delete your user account or unsubscribe from the Services.</p>

<p>Some of our service providers may assist us with the secure hosting, processing or transcription of online meeting recordings. Such providers may be located abroad, in which case the section "<strong>How do we protect your personal data</strong>" applies.</p>

<p>In some cases, the organisations we work with may act as data controllers of your personal data. In particular, third parties that assist us with the serving of advertisements. These third parties are typically governed by their own terms of service and privacy policies, which we strongly recommend you read.</p>

<p>A list of our main service providers (including, for each service provider, their contact information) is provided in Annex 1 of this Privacy Policy.</p>

<h4><strong>4. Events-related services, fan engagement opportunities and other initiatives</strong></h4>

<p>Our Services can be used to register for and participate in surveys, games, contests, sweepstakes or other fan engagement opportunities, to apply for registration or accreditation to attend the Olympic Games or other events organised by us, or for booking travel and accommodation in relation to such initiatives.</p>

<p>In certain situations, your use of those Services may entail you sharing personal data directly, or require us to share your personal data, with third parties. For example, travel or accommodation providers, providers of prize promotion administration and prize fulfilment services, academic institutions, governmental agencies, members of the Olympic Movement (International Federations, National Olympic Committees or OCOGs…), third parties authorised to launch and operate Olympic-themed digital services, and other entities involved in the delivery of an event or other initiative. User-facing information relevant to the event or initiative may include supplementary information about these third parties.</p>

<h4><strong>5. Offers and services from our partners</strong></h4>

<p>From time to time, we will offer you the possibility to receive services and communications (including communications related to products and services) from selected third parties, such as our commercial partners and other constituents of the Olympic Movement. In case you opt in to such services or communications (or can otherwise lawfully receive communications from them), we will share your personal data with these organisations, who will process your personal data as a separate data controller.</p>

<p>Upon your consent, we transfer your email address to the International Paralympic Committee (“<strong>IPC</strong>”) for the purpose of promotional communications about the Paralympic Games, the Paralympic Movement and the related initiatives of IPC partners. The IPC will process your personal data as a separate data controller where you decide to subscribe to the IPC’s promotional communications. Should you wish to opt-out of the IPC’s promotional communications, please contact the IPC directly.</p>

<h4><strong>6. Legal disclosure</strong></h4>

<p>We reserve the right to disclose personal data we hold about you if we are required to do so under applicable laws or pursuant to any judicial or administrative process and, to the extent necessary, to investigate, prevent, or take actions in relation to unlawful activities or a violation of our Terms of Service.</p>
<h3><strong>How do we protect your personal data?</strong></h3>

<h4><strong>1. Data security</strong></h4>

<p>We use technical and organisational measures to protect your personal data against the risks of damage, destruction, loss or unauthorised access, in accordance with applicable laws.</p>

<h4><strong>2. International transfer</strong></h4>

<p>We may process your personal data in a territory other than your place of residence. We adopt measures as required under applicable law to ensure your data will be given the relevant protection.</p>

<p>The personal data we collect will usually be processed in the European Union, the United Kingdom or in Switzerland (which provides a level of protection equivalent to the European Economic Area according to the European Commission Decision of 26 July 2000). We may, however, transfer your personal data to third parties for the purposes and legal basis for processing highlighted in this Privacy Policy (see the section above ‘<strong>Who do we share your information with?’</strong>). Some of these third parties may be based in countries that, like the United States of America, do not provide in their laws for a level of protection of your privacy equivalent to that applied within the European Union and Switzerland. We adopt measures as required under applicable law to ensure your data will be given the relevant protection. Before transferring data from Switzerland or the European Union to other countries, we implement safeguard mechanisms recognised by Swiss and European regulators, in particular standard contractual clauses. Alternatively, if we transfer personal data to organisations that participate in the ‘Data Privacy Framework’ as developed by the U.S. Department of Commerce and the European Commission, UK Government, and Swiss Federal Administration, such framework provides us with a legal mechanism to make that transfer.</p>

<h4><strong>3. Age limitation</strong></h4>

<p>Users who are not of legal age for data protection purposes or for the purposes of receiving our Services (according to the laws of the territory in which they reside) must obtain the consent of their parent or legal guardian before using our Services and the IOC reserves the right to request proof of such consent and/or of the age of the user at any time in case of any doubt. You can learn more about our age requirements for data protection purposes here: <a href="https://olympics.com/en/age-consent">https://olympics.com/en/age-consent</a>. If you become aware that your child has provided us with personal data without your consent, please contact us.</p>

<h4><strong>4. Data retention</strong></h4>

<p>We will retain your personal data only for the duration necessary for the purposes identified in this Privacy Policy or as required to meet our legal requirements.</p>

<p>Where your personal data has been collected through a section of the Olympics.com website or associated mobile application dedicated to a specific edition of the Games, and where necessary to achieve its long-term mission to promote Olympic Movement and preserve the legacy of the Games and maintain user engagement, the IOC may continue to process such personal data even after the relevant OCOG (such as the Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games as established by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and the Japanese Olympic Committee) has stopped its own processing of the data. The IOC will continue to process your personal data in accordance with this Privacy Policy.</p>

<p>Identity-verification confirmations of athletes using the A365 Platform, or that have been collected otherwise through other programmes or initiatives (such as AATG), may be retained for as long as they remain necessary to determine whether a user is an athlete and to assess their eligibility for AATG programmes or for any other offers, services or initiatives reserved for athletes. If no such initiative is offered, or if an athlete does not participate in or apply to any athlete-related initiative for a reasonable amount of time, the verification confirmation will be deleted, as it will no longer appear required for the relevant purposes. In such cases, athletes may be required to reconfirm their identity through the relevant verification processes, as mentioned herein, when they are offered, or choose to participate in, a subsequent athlete-related initiative.</p>
<h3><strong>Legal basis for processing your personal data and your rights</strong></h3>

<p>We mainly process your information to perform our obligations under the Terms of Service (or other terms that are presented at the point of personal data collection) but, in certain cases, we rely on an alternative legal basis. We have detailed below the legal bases on which we process your personal data.</p>

<p>Please note, however, that we adapt our legal basis for processing if the laws of the jurisdiction where you reside require us to do so. In particular, in territories where we must rely on a legal basis other than what is detailed in this section, your acceptance of this Privacy Policy constitutes your consent to the data processing activities described herein. </p>

<h4><strong>1. Contractual necessity</strong></h4>

<p>Contractual necessity applies where you accept our Terms of Service or other set of terms that are presented at the point of data collection and applicable to the Services, and justifies our processing of personal data in the course of the following activities:</p>

<p>a) providing the Services. For example, user accounts, and games, contests, sweepstakes or other fan engagement opportunity which we make available through the Services;  </p>

<p>b) securing and developing the Services;  </p>

<p>c) communicating with you in relation to the Services;  </p>

<p>d) sharing data with selected third parties who may provide you with their services;</p>

<p>e) transferring, storing or processing your data outside of Switzerland, the United Kingdom or the European Union, including within the United States of America and other countries;  </p>

<p>f) providing you with accreditation, accommodation, transport and other services or information which you have requested from us;</p>

<p>g) assessing, investigating and enforcing compliance with applicable terms and conditions contracted with us;</p>

<p>h) verifying your identity and confirming your eligibility as an athlete in order to provide you with access to athlete-specific features, services, or initiatives, including those available through the A365 Platform; and</p>

<p>i) recording and, where applicable, transcribing online meetings where this is necessary to document discussions related to the Services or to fulfil our contractual obligations.  </p>

<p>In these cases, you have the right to port your data.</p>

<h4><strong>2. Consent</strong></h4>

<p>Where you have expressly provided your prior consent, we will:</p>

<p>a) process your personal data to send you marketing communications (including via email);</p>

<p>b) process your personal data to carry out profiling activities in order to better understand fans of the Olympic Games and segment them according to their characteristics and preferences. This enables us to deliver tailored marketing communications to you (where you have consented to receive such communications) as well as more relevant online advertising or other content (in accordance with your consent to cookies), and find audiences of potential fans with similar interests and characteristics who may be interested in the Olympic Games as well as Olympic-themed products and services;</p>

<p>c) share your personal data with third parties for their own marketing purposes;</p>

<p>d) if we have procured your consent to the use of cookies, tracking pixels or similar technologies, collect your personal data via such cookies or similar technologies, and combine or further process such personal data as described in this Privacy Policy and our Cookie Policy; and</p>

<p>e) create recordings or transcriptions of online meetings where this is necessary to document discussions related to the Services or to fulfil our contractual obligations.</p>

<p>f) use tracking pixels or similar technologies, where required by applicable law and where you have expressly provided your prior consent.</p>

<p>In these cases, you have the right to port your data and to withdraw your consent.</p>

<h4><strong>3. Legitimate interests</strong></h4>

<p>We rely on our legitimate interests to process personal data in the course of the following activities:</p>

<p>a) distributing publicly available information related to the Olympic Games, Youth Olympic Games, Olympians and other athletes, sports and news stories via the Services;</p>

<p>b) securing and developing the Services;</p>

<p>c) communicating with you about the Services;</p>

<p>d) providing you with the Services that you have requested;</p>

<p>e) combining the personal data that you provide to us with data derived from marketing and advertising cookies, as well as the information we receive from third parties, and using that data to carry out profiling activities, to the extent consent is not legally required and after having assessed that your rights and interests are not overridden by such processing. The profiling activities are described in the section above entitled ‘<strong>How do we use the information we collect?</strong>’. As part of its marketing strategy for the long-term promotion of the Olympic Movement and the protection of its legacy, the IOC has a legitimate interest to better understand and find ways to develop its relationship with, and to reach its, existing and potential fans;</p>

<p>Residents of Italy - If you are a resident of Italy who consented to receive marketing communications, we will group you according to certain preferences and characteristics (for example, your date of birth, country of residence, favourite sport, favourite National Olympic Committee, and language) in order to determine which of our communications may be of interest to you. We can then send you marketing communications that are more relevant to those preferences and characteristics. If you did not consent to marketing communications, we will not use your data for this purpose. We do not intend for this use of data to be intrusive: we will only use a few of your preferences and characteristics, and the purpose of the activity is to improve fan engagement (taking into account your rights and interests);</p>

<p>f) evaluating the performance of the Services as well as third party sites and services;</p>

<p>g) carrying out internal commercial and operational reporting;</p>

<p>h) fulfilment of our role in, and optimising, the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games;</p>

<p>i) assessing, investigating and enforcing compliance with applicable terms and conditions agreed upon by third parties, such as OCOGs;  </p>

<p>j) establishing, protecting, and enforcing our rights and claims, including intellectual property and other legal rights;</p>

<p>k) promoting and raising awareness of the Olympic Movement, the Olympic Games and Paralympic Games, and our marketing partners;</p>

<p>l) ensuring the integrity of athlete-only programs and preventing misuse or fraud of athlete-specific initiatives, including by verifying the identity and eligibility of users claiming athlete status; and</p>

<p>m) conducting background checks and other appropriate verifications where necessary to comply with the relevant standards, regulations or terms, or with our integrity and compliance obligations, and to mitigate legal, reputational, or operational risks in connection with our activities or initiatives.</p>

<p>In these cases, you have the right to object to the processing of your information or ask us to restrict such processing.</p>

<h4><strong>4. Compliance with our legal obligations</strong></h4>

<p>We may also invoke our legal obligations as a valid ground for sharing your information with judiciary or law enforcement authorities, if we are ever obliged to do so and according to applicable laws.</p>

<p>In such case, you have the right to object to the processing of your information or ask us to restrict such processing.</p>
